opd_prescribing_evidence: Indian pharmacogenetic studies report CYP2C19*2 allele frequency ~46% in a South Indian ASPCR cohort with reduced clopidogrel antiplatelet efficacy in carriers (PMID 36960518); a South Asian Indian case-control study (1191 subjects) confirmed CYP2C19 variants associate with acute coronary syndrome risk and clopidogrel response (PMID 37985132). A cross-sectional cardiovascular OPD study assessed prescribing trends and rational use patterns including antiplatelets (PMID 40162464).
notes: Clopidogrel is a very commonly prescribed antiplatelet in Indian cardiology/OPD post-ACS and post-stenting care.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for specific % in retrieved Indian OPD studies; not listed among top agents in the schizophrenia OPD study (risperidone/olanzapine dominant, PMID 35481315).
notes: Increasingly used but behind risperidone/olanzapine in Indian OPD psychiatry.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND; hydrocodone is not a marketed/available opioid formulation in India (scheduling restrictions).
notes: Not available/marketed in India — irrelevant to Indian prescribing.

opd_prescribing_evidence: Indian prospective TB cohort study measured serum isoniazid levels and treatment response under the national TB program regimen (PMID 38589119); isoniazid is a cornerstone drug of India's NTEP/RNTCP program used in nearly all pulmonary TB OPD patients nationally.
notes: Isoniazid is an extremely commonly prescribed drug in Indian primary care given the very high TB burden and universal use in first-line ATT regimens under the national TB elimination program.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for India OPD/oncology prescribing frequency; tegafur-based combinations have limited availability in India.
notes: Rarely used in Indian oncology practice compared to capecitabine/5-FU.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for India OPD prescribing frequency.
notes: Cardiology specialist antiarrhythmic; rarely initiated in primary care in India.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for a specific India OPD %; aminoglycosides used mainly for MDR-TB and hospital-acquired infections.
notes: Predominantly hospital/injectable use in India (including MDR-TB regimens); uncommon in routine outpatient primary care.

opd_prescribing_evidence: The largest Indian pharmacogenomic dataset in this CPIC list: NUDT15 c.415C>T variant genotyping was shown to better predict azathioprine-induced leucopenia than TPMT in a prospective cohort of 1014 Indian IBD patients (PMID 33111378); a case-control study in Eastern India examined TPMT/NUDT15 and azathioprine-induced leukopenia (PMID 39078179).
notes: Commonly prescribed by gastroenterologists/rheumatologists for IBD and autoimmune disease across India; substantial India-specific pharmacogenomic evidence exists (NUDT15 more relevant than TPMT in South Asians).

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for India-specific OPD prescribing frequency.
notes: Used mainly in oncology antiemetic protocols in India; less common than ondansetron in general OPD.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for specific India OPD %; abacavir (with HLA-B*57:01 screening) is used in NACO ART regimens, especially pediatric/second-line.
notes: Used within India's HIV ART program; HLA-B*57:01 testing not yet standard in India due to cost/low allele frequency in South Asians.

opd_prescribing_evidence: Psychiatry OPD drug-utilization study: amitriptyline was the most commonly prescribed drug for depression at 34.9% (PMID 24551631). A neurology OPD RCT in West Bengal used amitriptyline 25mg as a standard monotherapy comparator for neuropathic pain, confirming routine primary-care use (PMID 31736565).
notes: Amitriptyline is a very commonly prescribed TCA in Indian OPD, both for depression and (at low dose) neuropathic pain/migraine prophylaxis.

opd_prescribing_evidence: Indian IBD studies on NUDT15/TPMT genotyping and thiopurine-induced leukopenia are extensive (PMID 33111378: 1014 IBD patients; PMID 39078179: case-control leukopenia study), reflecting real clinical thiopurine use in India, though mercaptopurine itself is more often used in pediatric oncology (ALL) than azathioprine's IBD/rheum indications.
notes: Used mainly in pediatric oncology (ALL maintenance) in India; specialist-prescribed, not primary-care OPD.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for a specific India OPD %; ondansetron is a very commonly used antiemetic across Indian OPD (gastroenteritis, chemotherapy-induced nausea, pregnancy-related nausea) and emergency departments.
notes: Very commonly prescribed antiemetic in Indian primary care and OPD across multiple indications.

opd_prescribing_evidence: NO_DATA_FOUND for India-specific prescribing frequency; thioguanine shares TPMT/NUDT15 pharmacogenomics with mercaptopurine/azathioprine.
notes: Rarely used in current Indian oncology practice; largely superseded by mercaptopurine in ALL regimens.
